research_question: Can a shared Mamba-2 forecaster with train-only signed-ACF relation supervision and a lightweight cross-variable token branch match strong forecasting baselines without claiming universal Mamba superiority?
primary_hypothesis: The cross-variable token branch is more likely to recover multivariate forecasting accuracy than a plain shared temporal scan; for a causal memory, train-only ACF peak strength should be combined with legal forecast-step availability. Signed ACF supervision remains a separate objective and may help only when train-split periodic structure is stable.

arms.purpose: direct Mamba forecaster without auxiliary branches
train-only dominant signed-ACF strength order for variable tokens
channel-specific temporal control for high-dimensional data
historical fixed-lag causal ACF residual control
horizon-step-specific reliability for legal ACF memory

acf_contract.lag_selection: train_peaks_available uses train-only peak strength times legal forecast-step fraction; resolved lags are horizon-specific and persisted in run metadata

primary_analysis: paired seed delta in scaled MSE against PatchTST and against MambaACF plain
channel-structure controls: shared, channel-independent, variable-token, and variable-order permutation
95 percent paired confidence interval and Wilcoxon signed-rank sensitivity
Holm and BH-FDR correction across dataset-horizon comparisons
parameter count, peak allocated/reserved GPU memory, end-to-end epoch time, and device-resident latency
channel-level error distribution for Electricity and Traffic

stopping_and_reporting.publication_claim_boundary: No claim of universal Mamba superiority or speed advantage unless all registered comparisons support it.
